metadata.rules_text:
- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a significant price spike, model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% for the next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices; adjust forecast mean by subtracting 2–5% of recent 7-day average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 14-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend after a dip, model often underreacts; increase forecast slope by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days following the dip.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overweights recent high prices; use 30-day moving average as baseline for smoothing out short-term volatility.
